I took my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout all the lands of Israel’s inheritance, because they had committed sin and wickedness in Israel.
Look, all of you are Israelites. Give your judgment and advice about this.”
All the people rose as one and said, “None of us will go to his tent, and none of us will turn aside to his house.
Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: we will cast lots against it.

We will take ten men out of every hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to obtain provisions for the people who are crossing over to go against Gibeah in Benjamin, in response to all the wickedness they have committed in Israel.”
All the men of Israel gathered against the town as one, united.
All the tribes of Israel sent men to all the people of Benjamin, saying, “What is this evil that has happened among you?
Now hand over the wicked men who are in Gibeah, so that we may kill them and remove the evil from Israel.” But the Benjaminites were unwilling to listen to their fellow Israelites.
All the Benjaminites gathered from their towns at Gibeah to go out and fight against the Israelites.
On that day the Benjaminites from the towns were counted: twenty-six thousand men armed with swords, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were counted as seven hundred men,
whose right hands were disabled. Every one of them could sling a stone at a hair without missing.
The men of Israel, apart from the Benjaminites, were counted as four hundred thousand men armed with swords, all of them fighting men.
They set out and went up to Bethel and inquired of God. The Israelites said, “Who should go up first for us to fight against the Benjaminites?” The Lord said, “Judah first.”
The Israelites rose in the morning and camped against Gibeah.
The Benjaminites came out of Gibeah and lined up against Israel. On that day, when they fought against them, they struck down twenty-two thousand men of Israel to the ground.
The Israelites rallied again and once more drew up their battle line in the place where they had drawn it up on the first day.

The Israelites went up and wept before the Lord until evening. They asked the Lord, saying, “Shall we again go into battle against the Benjaminites, our brothers?” The Lord said, “Go up against them.”
The Israelites fought against the Benjaminites on the next day.
The Benjaminites came out of Gibeah against them on the second day, and again the Benjaminites struck down eighteen thousand men of Israel to the ground, all of them armed with swords.

All the Israelites and all the people went up and came to Bethel. They wept and sat there before the Lord. They fasted that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
The Israelites inquired of the Lord. The ark of the Lord was there in those days,

and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, served before him in those days. They said, “Should we go out again to battle against the Benjaminites, our brothers, or should we stop?” The Lord said, “Go up, because tomorrow I will hand them over to you.”
The Israelites set an ambush against Gibeah and surrounded it.
The Israelites went up against the Benjaminites on the third day and took up their positions against Gibeah as before.

The Benjaminites came out to meet the army and were drawn away from the town. As before, they began killing some of the men along the roads—one leading up to Gibeah and the other to Bethel—and in the open country, about thirty men of Israel.
The Benjaminites said, “They are being defeated before us as before.” But the Israelites said, “Let us flee and draw them out of the town onto the roads.”
All the Israelites rose from their positions and took up battle formation at Baal-tamar, while the Israelites lying in ambush emerged from their position, from the cave at Gibeah.
Ten thousand picked men from all Israel came opposite Gibeah, and the fighting grew fierce. The Benjaminites did not know that disaster had overtaken them.
The Lord defeated Benjamin before Israel, and that day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all of them armed with swords.
The Benjaminites saw that they were defeated. The Israelites had given ground to the men of Benjamin because they trusted the men they had placed in ambush against Gibeah.
The men lying in ambush fell quietly upon Gibeah. They advanced and put the whole town to the sword.
The men of Israel had arranged with those lying in ambush that they should send up a rising column of smoke from the town.
The men of Israel turned away from the battle, and Benjamin began killing men of Israel, thirty men, for they said, “They are certainly being defeated before us, as in the earlier battles.”
Smoke began to rise from the city like a pillar. The Benjaminites turned to look behind them, and there was the city’s cloud of smoke rising to heaven.
Then the men of Israel turned against them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified because they saw that disaster had come upon them.
They fled before the Israelites toward the wilderness road, but the battle overtook them, and those who were there before [?] them in the middle.
They pursued Benjamin and drove them away, destroying them with ease as far as the area opposite Gibeah on the east.
Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them fighting men.

They turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. Five thousand sword-bearing men fell along the roads. The Israelites pursued them as far as Gibeon and killed two thousand more of them.
In all, twenty-five thousand sword-bearing men of Benjamin fell that day, all of them valiant men.
Six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and stayed at the rock of Rimmon for four months.

The Israelites turned against the Benjaminites and put them to the sword, completely destroying them in the towns—people, livestock, and everything they found. They also burned down every town they found.
The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter as a wife to a Benjaminite.”
They came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening. They raised their voices and wept bitterly.
They said, “Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?”
The next day the people rose early, built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

The Israelites said, “Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come up to the assembly before the LORD?” For they had made a solemn oath that anyone who did not come up before the LORD at Mizpah must certainly be put to death.
The Israelites grieved over their brothers the Benjaminites and said, “Today one tribe has perished from Israel.”
They said, “What shall we do for those who remain without wives, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them wives?”
They said, “Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come up before the LORD at Mizpah?” No men from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp.
The people were counted there, and no one from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was found there.
And the people sent twelve thousand warriors there and commanded them, saying, “Go and put the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead to the sword, including the women and children.”
This is what you must do: destroy every man and every woman who has had sexual relations with a man.
Among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had never had sexual relations with men. They brought them to the camp at Shiloh, in the land of Canaan.
The whole assembly sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.
The Benjaminites returned at that time, and they gave them the women they had kept alive from among the women of Jabesh-gilead, but there were not enough for them.
And the people grieved for Benjamin, because the Lord had made a gap among the tribes of Israel.
The elders of the people said, “What shall we do for those who are left without wives, those who remain, since the women of Benjamin have perished?”
They said, “A remnant of Benjamin must be preserved, so that a tribe is not lost from Israel.
For we cannot give them wives from our daughters, because the Israelites swore, saying, ‘Cursed is anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.’”
They said, “Look, there is a recurring festival of the Lord at Shiloh, north of Bethel, east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”
They instructed the Benjaminites, saying to them, “Go and lie in wait in the vineyards.

When you see some of the daughters of Shiloh coming out to play tambourines, come out of the vineyards and seize a wife for yourselves, one for each man, from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

If their fathers or brothers come to plead their case before us, we will say to them, ‘Have mercy on them, because they did not each take a wife in battle. You did not give the women to them, so you have not sinned.’”
The Benjaminites did so and took wives for all of themselves from the women playing tambourines whom they seized. They returned to their inheritance, rebuilt the towns, and lived in them.
At that time the Israelites left there, each going to his tribe and his clan. They departed from there, each to his inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel, and everyone did whatever seemed right in his own eyes.
